summary: Capacity mining of retained Physics Lab runtime synthesis PR #408 exact head d31c100c5d3766ca14d89b046fff4cdb09086754 found an unbounded malformed entity-recipe key boundary: assertCanonicalRecipe checks only that entityRecipe.key is a string before using the caller-sized string as a canonical-map lookup key and, on miss, interpolating the complete value into the unknown-key assertion diagnostic. PhysicsLabRecipe has no upstream entity-key byte ceiling. An arbitrarily large forged string therefore forces hash/compare work proportional to malformed input and can make the failure diagnostic/temporary allocation scale with that input even though no canonical key can be that large. This is distinct from the already-recorded outer recipe-shape finding and from WorldEntity canonical-record metadata budgeting.
evidence: Inspected PR #408 exact source head d31c100c5d3766ca14d89b046fff4cdb09086754. assertCanonicalRecipe reads entityRecipe.key, asserts only type(entityKey) == 'string', then performs CANONICAL_ENTITIES_BY_KEY[entityKey] and asserts canonical ~= nil with a diagnostic containing the full entityKey.

Inspected PhysicsLabRecipe at the same exact head. Entity recipe keys are typed as string and generated from a fixed canonical set, but the recipe contract exposes no maximum byte length or validator that would reject oversized candidate keys before PhysicsLabRuntime receives them.

The canonical entity key set is finite and trusted, so a candidate longer than the longest canonical key is provably unable to match; preflighting against a ceiling derived from the canonical keys can reject impossible oversized input before hash lookup without inventing a new external protocol limit.

The existing runtime-recipe-shape finding evt-20260811-231200-s6r4n8q2-runtime-recipe-shape concerns unknown outer/table fields and ignored map entries, not entity-key byte cost. The 2026-08-12 WorldEntity metadata-budget finding concerns retained record metadata, not this runtime recipe-key failure path.

Current PhysicsLabRealizer constructs the canonical recipe internally, so this mining result does not claim a demonstrated current remote exploit, Workspace divergence, or engine failure. It hardens the public runtime constructor boundary for malformed/future-adapter input.
No production code was changed, no executable test was run by this worker, and no Roblox Studio, viewport, contact, diagnostics-capture, or two-client authority evidence is claimed.

metadata.recommendedNext: When the runtime-synthesis lineage is writable again, derive a trusted maximum canonical entity-key byte length from the canonical key set, reject candidates beyond it before table lookup, keep the rejection diagnostic bounded/content-independent, and add an adversarial Lune regression proving oversized rejection is fail-atomic before registry/fidelity authority registration. Preserve normal canonical and bounded unknown-key behavior.
